findings.quote: It s called Captain Crunch, he said quickly, as if speed would help. I named it when I was eight. After a cereal.
findings.claim: The reader is told he is embarrassed and told the name is silly, and Elena is kind about it. The kindness lands; the joke does not. This is the one place in the novel where a laugh was available.
findings.fix: Put the comedy in Elena s reply - taking the name completely seriously is funnier than any joke he could make.
findings.reference: prose characteristic, major; and the commissioned tone, warm funny and a little brave

findings.quote: she was still looking back at the hill as if she were reading its story, as if the earth had given up more than just a fossil and now she was reading what it meant
findings.claim: reading twice in one sentence, after two earlier uses and a turning something over three lines before. The image was specific when it belonged to her hands and the fossils; stretched over her mind and the hill and the earth it goes slack.
findings.fix: End on something concrete - the sun on the stones, her face, the hill.

findings.quote: She didn t laugh-not in the bad way, not in any way at all.
findings.claim: not in any way at all already contains not in the bad way

findings.quote: it caught the stones of the path and the stones of the dry-stone wall that ran down the slope
findings.claim: the stones of repeats inside one clause
It is immediately followed by That s a good name, she said, so Elena asks a question and speaks again with no reply from him between. Created by the attempt-2 patch.
findings.fix: one short answer from him between the two lines
findings.reference: prose characteristic, minor; introduced by the attempt-2 patch

iterations.notes: all four resolved. The critic judged the joke now lands - Does it crunch? engages the silliness as charming rather than stupid, and a ten-year-old would laugh. One new minor created by that same patch.
